neighbours.label: A predicate or continuation immediately following the word life
fire: Life is too short to spend every evening worrying.
Her life was suddenly much easier after the move.
Life goes on even after a painful disappointment.
He wanted his life to become more peaceful.
Life can be unpredictable when you travel so often.
The accident made her life a constant struggle.
She believes life will get better after graduation.
The poster reads Life In The Quiet Lane above a photograph.
quiet: Time is too short to spend every evening worrying.
Her work was suddenly much easier after the move.
Work goes on even after a painful disappointment.
He wanted his home to become more peaceful.
Work can be unpredictable when you travel so often.
The accident made her recovery a constant struggle.
She believes things will get better after graduation.
The poster reads Days In The Quiet Lane above a photograph.

notes: Both ordinary prose and titles contain strong post-life peaks. This is a lexical context claim rather than a claim about existence in general. No exploratory scoring; no downloaded band scan covers this unit. Sentences written by Codex.
